reason: Isolating the uplink starts the rehearsal of the local rack without Meridian.
expectation: I expect the shared controls to be disconnected from the corporate uplink so their local operation can be tested.

alternatives.reason: Testing the clinic link also matters, but I want to isolate the uplink first.

effect: The uplink is disconnected, but the green indicator alone does not establish that local services work.
reaction: The distinction makes me curious about the actual link test.
reason: Testing the clinic radio link is the only available combination and checks a useful path during the outage.
expectation: I expect the offline handset to test whether clinic calls can still travel over the local radio link.

effect: The radio link works, but clinic calls depend on the company directory for address lookup; the controller may provide a local alternative.
reaction: The working road and missing signpost is a clear, surprising failure.
reason: The only available combination may let the controller supply the clinic's local address.
expectation: I expect a local directory or address setting to help the handset find the clinic, though it may need further testing.

effect: The handset now has local directory settings and can configure the rack through its service port; the fix still needs applying and testing.
reaction: The limited local address list makes the proposed fix feel concrete.
reason: The only available combination applies the local directory settings to the disconnected rack.
expectation: I expect the rack to use the local directory without Meridian, though clinic calls will still need a test.

effect: The rack now runs its own directory without the uplink, but clinic calls and water still need checking.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the missing directory restored locally.
reason: The only available combination may test the handset against the rack's local directory.
expectation: I expect the handset to find local services through the rack, though the clinic call may need a separate test.

effect: The handset resolves the clinic locally and Eli answers, confirming the call path works without the uplink; water still needs checking.
reaction: Eli's insistence on a callback is a nice, practical touch.
reason: The only available combination should check the water service alongside the working clinic call.
expectation: I expect a rehearsal check showing whether water remains available while the clinic link operates locally.

effect: Ren's coordinated stop-and-restart test confirmed that local pump control, water and reporting survived without the uplink; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The test was satisfying because it checked the actual service rather than relying on an indicator.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the clinic call and then coordinating the pump test made the repair meaningful: both communication and water worked without the uplink.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading the directory settings and then applying them felt a little procedural, especially with only one combination available at each step.

surprise.text: The radios could exchange packets while the clinic call failed because address lookup still depended on the company directory. The road-and-signpost explanation made the hidden dependency clear.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the directory setup was split into several forced combinations rather than meaningful choices.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the locally controlled services fare during the migration, although this chapter's mostly forced sequence offered limited decision-making.
